_comment: End-to-end timelines of the whole bridge (src/app.js and everything it wires together) against a fake panel and a real MQTT broker (Mosquitto 2, a private instance per scenario that knows the user bridge/secret, which the bridge's MQTT_USERNAME/MQTT_PASSWORD name, and holds no retained message at the start). Each row of a group is one scenario: the bridge is started, then 'steps' are played in order. Setup: 'login' holds the bridge env USERNAME/PASSWORD, the session value the panel hands out and the u/p the panel accepts for that session (an independent copy of a crypto.json vector, so this file stays self-contained); panel has requireLogin on and the default six zones Predsien, Lava izba, Prava izba, Spalna, Obyvacka, Chodba, status tables of 32 zeros, useraccess [1, 0]; time is simulated: 'advance_ms' moves the clock of the bridge's own timers (poll 1000 ms, keep-alive 3000 ms, MQTT connect timeout 5000 ms) and then waits for the real network effects. Row keys: name, known_bug?, note?, panel?, broker?, start?, steps?. panel: zones ([enabled, name] pairs), statuszone, useraccess, accept_login (false: every login is rejected), down (true: panel is not reachable at startup), faults (list of {path, kind, times?} active from the start; times omitted = for ever). Fault kinds: http_500 (HTTP 500), reset (connection reset before any response), hang (request never answered), login_page (HTTP 200 with the login page), garbage (HTTP 200 with a page that has no status tables), wrong_title (HTTP 200 with a well-formed page titled something else than 'Paradox IP Module'), page (HTTP 200 with the fault's own 'page': an inline string or {file: path relative to tests/}). broker: accept_credentials (false: the credentials the bridge is configured with are unknown to the broker, which refuses the login: CONNACK 5 'not authorised' on Mosquitto, where MQTT 3.1.1 also allows 4 'bad username or password'), silent (the broker accepts the connection and never answers CONNECT), down (true: nothing listens on the broker port), retained ({topic: payload} the broker already holds, published retained by another client before the bridge starts, replayed on SUBSCRIBE). start: ready (default true: wait until the REST port accepts connections; false: startup is expected to fail or hang) and expect (checked once startup is over). Step actions, applied in this order within a step: panel_status ({statuszone?, useraccess?, alarms?} the panel serves from now on), panel_fault (same shape as a fault), panel_expire_session, panel_down, broker_drop_clients (the broker disconnects the bridge's session; the user stays valid), mqtt_command ('arm' | 'disarm' | {topic, payload}: 'arm' is topic paradox/command/arm with an empty payload; published, QoS 0 and not retained, by another client to the broker, which delivers it to the bridge's subscription), mqtt_message ({topic, payload}: a PUBLISH written into the bridge's connection as if the broker had sent it, even for a topic the bridge did not subscribe to, which a real broker never delivers), signal (SIGHUP | SIGINT | SIGTERM delivered to the process), rest ({method, path} request to the bridge's REST API), advance_ms. Expectations (expect) describe what happened DURING that step, i.e. since the previous check; absent keys mean 'nothing': mqtt_published (messages the bridge published, in order, as another client subscribed to paradox/# sees them on the broker; all are QoS 0, retained as listed: the flag the bridge set; the broker's own log of the bridge's PUBLISH packets must show the same topics, QoS, retain flags and payload lengths, so nothing is published anywhere else either), panel_requests (request lines the panel received, in order; at startup absent means not checked), panel_requests_any_order (the same compared as a multiset, for timers firing in the same tick), panel_request_counts ({request line: how many times}, for long stretches of time), process_exit (exit codes passed to process.exit, in order), logged_error (true: at least one error-level log entry was written during the step, false: none; log text is otherwise not contractual, but a failure described as 'only logged' must be logged), rest_response ({status, body?}; body is the parsed JSON, or the text for non-JSON), and, as absolute states at the end of the step, broker_connects (number of CONNECT packets the bridge has sent so far: the broker has answered each, accepted or refused; with silent, counted where the connection ends), broker_connacks (return codes of the CONNACKs the broker has sent so far, in order: 0 accepted, 5 not authorised), broker_subscriptions (topics subscribed so far, in order), broker_retained ({topic: payload, or null for none}: what a client subscribing now gets from the broker's retained store) and rest_listening (whether the REST port accepts connections). Besides, at the end of every scenario each topic the bridge published with retain holds the last such payload as the broker's retained message. Group missing_env is different: each row unsets the env variables in 'missing' and expects loading the bridge to throw an Error with expected_error before any I/O. A bug pinned on purpose carries known_bug (catalog id in tests/README.md). All message payloads are hand-written, nothing is computed by the code under test.

startup.name: login, then MQTT connect and two subscriptions, in this order; the REST port opens; nothing is published before the first poll
startup.note: The startup emissions of status_listener happen before anyone listens (initial armed=null, every sensor=false), so the broker sees no message at all until the first poll.

startup.name: no poll before 1000 ms, first poll at exactly 1000 ms
startup.note: The first poll publishes OFF only because the assumed initial armed state is null, not false.

startup.name: a panel with no enabled zone starts and still reports the armed state
a failing logout before login is tolerated
index page failures are retried and startup still succeeds
a retained command on the broker is executed as soon as the bridge subscribes
startup.note: The broker replays retained messages on SUBSCRIBE; the bridge acts on any message of a command topic, whatever the payload.

keep_alive.name: keep-alive request every 3000 ms with a bare msgid parameter
keep_alive.note: The random cache-buster parameter is dropped by axios because its value is null.

keep_alive.name: steady state: 30 s of an unchanged panel are 30 polls, 10 keep-alives and a single message
a keep-alive answered with HTTP 500 is only logged
keep_alive.note: Unlike a status poll, a keep-alive failure never reaches the exit handler.

keep_alive.name: a keep-alive with a reset connection is only logged
a keep-alive answered with the login page is not an error
keep_alive.note: The response body is never inspected, so an expired session goes unnoticed by the keep-alive.

armed.name: disarmed panel: OFF at the first poll, not repeated
armed.note: OFF is published only because the initial state is assumed to be null.

armed.name: armed panel: ON at the first poll, not repeated
unknown code at startup publishes nothing, a later known code publishes
codes 0 3 4 5 6 8 9 10 17 22 are all unknown and never publish
disarmed to arming to armed to disarmed: arming and armed are one state
a transition through an unknown code publishes nothing, then republishes the same state
armed.note: The retained message keeps the stale state while the code is unknown, and the return to the old state is published again.

armed.name: only area 1 matters: the second area never changes the published state
armed.note: useraccess is parsed with parseInt on an array, so only its first element counts.

armed.name: an empty useraccess table is an unknown state

sensors.name: closed sensors at startup publish nothing, whatever their code
sensors.note: The captured unarmed page has codes 5 and 6 on two zones; they start 'closed' like everything else.

sensors.name: a sensor opening publishes ON on its own topic and closing publishes OFF
only code 1 is open, every other code is closed
one poll with several changes publishes the armed state first, then sensors by ascending index
status entries beyond the enabled zones are never published
a sensor that opens and closes between two polls is never seen
a status table shorter than the zone list reads missing entries as closed
a status table with a single entry is read as an empty array of that length, so nothing opens
sensors.note: The table text new Array(1) is evaluated as is, and a lone number is a length, not an element.

sensors.name: a useraccess table with a single entry is an unknown state
sensors.note: new Array(2) is an empty array of length 2, not [2].

sensors.name: a disabled zone in front shifts every sensor onto the status entry of the position before it
sensors.note: Enabled zones are re-indexed after filtering: sensor/<position> reads statuszone[position], so the status of the disabled zone 0 is published as sensor/0 and the real zone 2 (Window) is never seen.

sensors.name: a disabled zone between enabled ones: the last enabled zone is read from the wrong entry
a zone flagged for area 2 or for both areas is not monitored, so sensors are numbered over the area 1 zones alone
sensors.note: The first number of a tbl_zone pair is an area bitmask (tests/README.md) and the bridge keeps only pairs equal to 1. Two of these four zones qualify, so only sensor/0 and sensor/1 exist, reading statuszone[0] and statuszone[1].

sensors.name: with 32 enabled zones only the first 16 are ever published
sensors.note: util.iterateTuples stops halfway: 64 list items yield 16 tuples.

sensors.name: with no enabled zone no sensor is ever published

mqtt_commands.name: arm command: panel is told to arm, the next poll publishes ON
disarm command: panel is told to disarm, the next poll publishes OFF
the payload of an arm command is ignored
mqtt_commands.note: Any message on paradox/command/arm arms, even OFF, disarm or an empty payload.

mqtt_commands.name: the payload of a disarm command is ignored
commands go out in the order received, always for area 00
messages on any other topic are ignored, exact topic match only
mqtt_commands.note: Delivered to the bridge's connection even though it never subscribed to them, as a misbehaving broker would.

mqtt_commands.name: a command failing with HTTP 500 is logged, not retried, and does not stop the bridge
a command with a reset connection is logged and does not stop the bridge
a command answered with the login page after session expiry counts as success
mqtt_commands.note: The response is ignored, so the lost session goes unnoticed and nothing is armed.

rest.name: GET /status returns the raw panel tables as JSON
GET /status always reports alarms [0], the alarm table is never parsed
POST /arm arms the panel and answers 200 OK
POST /disarm disarms the panel and answers 200 OK
arming over REST shows up as an armed message at the next poll
a panel answering HTTP 500 gives 500 with the error message, and the bridge keeps running
rest.note: The msg text is axios's own message; a port only needs a 500 with a msg field.

rest.name: a panel resetting the connection gives 500 with the transport error message
rest.note: 'socket hang up' is Node's text for a reset before any response.

rest.name: GET /status after session expiry fails to parse the login page and gives 500
POST /arm and /disarm after session expiry still answer 200 OK
unauthenticated POST /disarm disarms the alarm
rest.note: No credential of any kind is part of the request; the bridge also listens on all interfaces (checked in app.test.js).

rest.name: only GET /status, POST /arm and POST /disarm exist; everything else is 404 without touching the panel
express default routing: trailing slash, upper case, query string and HEAD reach the same handlers
rest.note: Incidental to Express defaults, not a requirement; a port may be stricter.

failures.name: a status poll answered with HTTP 500 exits with code 1
a status poll with a reset connection exits with code 1
a status poll answered with a page without the status tables exits with code 1
a panel that went away exits with code 1 at the next poll
an expired panel session exits with code 1 at the next poll
failures.note: The panel answers the login page; there is no re-login.

failures.name: the first failed poll is fatal even after many good ones
a poll that never gets an answer never times out and the next poll overlaps it
failures.note: No HTTP timeout and no in-flight guard: the second poll goes out while the first is still pending.

failures.name: losing the MQTT connection exits with code 1
wrong panel credentials exit with code 1 before MQTT or the REST server start
an unreachable panel exits with code 1 before MQTT or the REST server start
a login page request failing with HTTP 500 exits with code 1
a login page without a session value exits with code 1
a successful login answered with a pretty-printed default page cannot be recognised and exits with code 1
failures.note: The title regex does not span lines, so an indented multi-line head fails to match.

failures.name: a default page with another title means login failed and exits with code 1
a permanently failing index page is requested 11 times back to back, then exit code 1
failures.note: The retry helper ignores its wait time.

failures.name: a zone name with a hyphen makes the whole bridge fail to start
an unreachable broker is only noticed by the 5000 ms connect timeout, which exits with code 1
failures.note: A refused connection raises no error event on the MQTT client; it just keeps retrying.

failures.name: a broker rejecting the credentials exits with code 1 before the REST server and the pollers start
failures.note: A real broker closes the connection after refusing the login, and the MQTT client, which the bridge never ends (the KB-17 mechanism), redials from its own reconnect timer; the number of CONNECTs after a long wait depends on that timer and is not pinned. The bridge itself stays dead: no REST port, no polling, no publish.

failures.name: a broker that never answers CONNECT exits with code 1 after exactly 5000 ms, then the client keeps reconnecting
failures.note: The timeout rejects but never ends the MQTT client, so it retries in the background (the second CONNECT arrives with the client's own 30 s connect timeout).

shutdown.name: SIGTERM exits with 143 without logging out of the panel, then nothing runs any more
shutdown.note: exitHandler returns the logout function without calling it: no /logout.html after the one before login. The server is closed, both timers are stopped, and later status changes are not published.

shutdown.name: a signal right after startup, before the first poll, exits cleanly
a repeated or second signal runs the shutdown again and exits with its own code

missing_env.name: USERNAME and HOSTNAME unset: HOSTNAME is reported first
PASSWORD and USERNAME unset: USERNAME is reported first
PORT and PASSWORD unset: PASSWORD is reported first
MQTT_HOSTNAME and PORT unset: PORT is reported first
MQTT_PORT and MQTT_HOSTNAME unset: MQTT_HOSTNAME is reported first
MQTT_USERNAME and MQTT_PORT unset: MQTT_PORT is reported first
MQTT_PASSWORD and MQTT_USERNAME unset: MQTT_USERNAME is reported first
